items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Every time I see him I think of Buddy Johnson.

ctx.x: The whole seventh ward would be listening to Buddy. He played them dimished chords. They had never heard nothing like that. Playing Indian Sau Wau [or Indian Sagua]. You know Indian Sau Wau?

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Buddy Johnson. He had a big band, but he started with a little band. But all them little bands went around. It was a whole new concept of Black music.

ctx.x: Brown. What's that guy's name? Brown. Buddy...
